title: Again Our Ears Have Heard the Voice
description: Again Our Ears Have Heard the Voice in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 83 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “After Divine Service”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-gain our ears have heard the voice At which the dead shall live; O, may the sound our hearts re-joice, And strength im-mor-tal give!

lines: Again our ears have heard the voice
At which the dead shall live;
O, may the sound our hearts rejoice,
And have we heard the word with joy?
And have we felt its power?
To keep it be our blest employ,

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
